title: The Lottery That Lost Money to a Retired Shopkeeper
alts: He Found a Lottery That Paid More Than It Cost. Legally.
How a Retired Couple Won $27 Million From the Lottery With Maths
hook: They say the lottery is a tax on people who can't do maths. In 2003, a retired shopkeeper in Evart, Michigan did the maths, and found a lottery that was losing money to him. Over nine years, Jerry and Marge Selbee's group won almost $27 million in prizes. Legally.
open: A tax on people who can't do maths
sources: Jason Fagone, 'Jerry and Marge Go Large', HuffPost Highline (2018)

Wikipedia, 'Jerry and Marge Selbee' and 'Massachusetts Lottery' (Cash WinFall): $5M Winfall roll-down; $2M Cash WinFall roll-down; ~$27M in winning tickets; $7.75M profit; MIT group's $17M bet in 7 hours; game ended January 26, 2012
